REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  September 27, 2021

A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR HUFF at 7:04 P.M. via teleconference, pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20.
Committee Members Present:  Huff, Shinn, Ciarolla, Griggs, Harik, Nilsen
Committee Members Absent:  Brtis, Silvano, Robinson, Martin, Zigrang
City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager, Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor, Rosa Pinuelas
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  MEMBER HARIK moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN, to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE JUNE 28, 2021 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.
There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF so ordered.
AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN /ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
None.
STAFF ITEMS
A.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER (PWEC) CONTRACT RENEWAL
Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis provided an overview of the written staff report.
COMMITTEE MEMBER GRIGGS asked who funds capital projects at the Peter Weber
Equestrian Center facility. ACM Davis responded that the City pays for larger capital
projects to which CHAIR HUFF confirmed.
COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN stated that there may be challenges for parking if a new
arena is built. PWEC representative, Gil Houle, stated that he believes the organization
interested in seeing the arena built can invest into the project if it is approved to move
forward.
COMMITTEE MEMBER NILSEN asked if the Mane for Movement arena request was
proposed to be tabled indefinitely or as part of the contract extension discussion. She
further stated that she would like to see the City move forward with the proposal somehow
but agrees more information is needed. CHAIR HUFF responded that it would be
considered separately from the extension.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
SEPTEMBER 27, 2021
  1
 CHAIR HUFF received and filed with input provided for continued consideration.

B.  PUBLIC RIDING RING RULES REVIEW
ACM Davis provided an overview of the written staff report.
COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN agreed the Committee should consider reducing
restricted weekend hours and explained the impact to trainers when arenas are otherwise
not used for public recreation. Audience Member Pam Schachter provided historical input
on the Equestrian Committee decision and public recreation riding hours at Chandler
Arena. Discussion ensued explaining that the intent of the rules for Chandler Arena is to
provide only two trainers with two riders so recreational riders can access easier.
COMMITTEE MEMBER GRIGGS explained that the only real impact would be when
there are horse shows at Ernie Howlett and trainers need to move their lessons to
Chandler Arena.
It was recommended by the Committee to open up Chandler Arena for training all day
and not restrict hours for recreational use. Some discussion ensued on whether the Rules
should be adjusted so the restriction is for one hour instead of two hours but general
consensus was to eliminate the restricted hours completely.
ACM Davis explained that the Rules were established by Resolution and asked if the
Committee would like to open the use on a temporary basis with a report back to
determine if it should be updated permanently. She further explained she would confirm
what, if anything, is needed with the City Attorney. The Committee concurred.
CHAIR HUFF so ordered and requested that staff work inform trainers of this update.
COMMITTEE MEMBER NILSEN expressed concern related to rules for horse shows, as
Ernie Howlett does not have a listed limit within the Rules. She expressed concern
regarding the Portuguese Horse Show - where the ring closest to Hawthorne Boulevard
was being used for young riders and felt that there were too many horses at one time
causing safety concerns. She suggested that limits be set or recommended for events,
particularly for youth riders. COMMITTEE GRIGGS agreed that it could be a cause for
concern if there are too many in the ring. COMMITTEE MEMBER NILSEN stated she
reported the event organizer because the concern was alarming and that she did a survey
of customary beginner classes and found that groups are often split for eight to cantor.
She suggested that be a rule moving forward.
The Committee agreed that staff should look into this further. ACM Davis stated she
would look into what is standard protocol and see what can be done about establishing a
best practice or guide for horse shows renting the City’s facility.

  C.  HONORING DALE ALLEN (VERBAL REPORT)
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
SEPTEMBER 27, 2021
  2
 CHAIR HUFF honored Dale Allen, long time Rolling Hills Estates resident, City volunteer
and equestrian upon his passing in August. COMMITTEE MEMBERS GRIGGS and
SHINN also provided comments honoring Mr. Allen. ACM Davis shared that in years
past, the City honored Mr. Allen through a recognition plaque at City Hall, a round pen at
Dapplegray Park and a trail named after him, “Dale Trail.” Those interested in honoring
him further, may consider making a donation to the Palos Verdes Peninsula Horsemen’s
Association or City’s Pepper Tree Foundation in his memory.
D.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
COMMITTEE MEMBER NILSEN shared a concern related to the bobcat tractor falling
down the hill at Fern Creek trail near her neighbor’s property. COMMITTEE MEMBER
GRIGGS shared similar concerns and was curious why the work being done by the trail
is happening and asked if staff can clarify if that is City or private property. ACM Davis
responded that it was believed to be private property, formerly owned by the Fitzpatick
family, but further stated staff would confirm that work was all done on private property
with any necessary permits, if required.
E.  EQUESTRIAN RECOGNITION
ACM Davis reported that the City, through its Pepper Tree Foundation, has not yet
proceeded with the recognition bench for Jan Ball at Peter Weber Equestrian Center and
Carol Dean-Porter at Ernie Howlett judge's booth as a result of not receiving the level of
donations needed to cover the full cost of the recognitions. The Committee suggested
that staff inform the Palos Verdes Peninsula Horsemen’s Association to see if more
donations might come in.

COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

None.

B.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis explained that this item will become a standing item to provide an opportunity
for Committee members to share anything for future consideration and staff research.
COMMITTEE MEMBER NILSEN shared her personal experience of needing urgent
medical support for her horse and the obstacles she dealt with in identifying an emergency
after-hours vet and someone who could haul her horse to a hospital immediately. She
realized through this experience that there is no coordinated vet or hauling system and
suggested there be a list of commercial haulers posted on the City’s website, arenas,
barns and with private facilities as well as the consideration of on-call vet system.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
SEPTEMBER 27, 2021
  3
 COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN responded that often times haulers can be found but that
a list should be readily available and easily accessible. She further explained that the
emergency vet scenario is more difficult and it would be ideal if there could be a big space
available for urgent surgeries rather than hauling a horse far for emergencies.
Additionally, she suggested there be more education to the community on warning signs
of horse illnesses, like horse colic. COMMITTEE HARIK stated that if one can get a
trailer, than the emergency vet isn’t as needed.

ACM Davis suggested this item could be discussed as part of the equine emergency
preparedness effort and COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN suggested COMMITTEE
MEMBER NILSEN be added.

CHAIR HUFF asked staff to make sure a list of trailering and vets be added to the City
website.

CHAIR HUFF thanked COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN and other equestrian community
members for their involvement in the planning and implementation of a successful City
Celebration. COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN agreed and extended appreciation to Sean
Martin and John Arbuckle and other Committee members and staff for their help. She
suggested that next year a country western band and dancing be part of the activities.
COMMITTEE MEMBER HARIK added that it was a fun and well-attended event. CHAIR
HUFF suggested that the band be considered and possibly a dinner for future years.
ACM Davis responded that the ideas will be part of the future debrief discussion.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HARIK reported that she participated in a horse show at Ernie
Howlett Park and the sand was very deep in the turn out arena between the dressage
and other two arenas and that she was concerned. COMMITTEE MEMBER GRIGGS
stated that Superintendent Goldsmith had informed her that watering the arena helps
make it less deep but she reported that it needs a lot more water than the sprinkler
provides in one use. COMMITTEE MEMBER HARIK explained that she was not aware
of the water option. Audience Member Schachter explained that this was an issue for the
Portuguese Horse Show too and they get a water truck for their event. Discussion ensued
about ways to make sure this arena is properly watered in advance of uses, including the
consideration of purchasing a City water truck. ACM Davis responded that she would
speak with Superintendent Goldsmith to review options.

Audience Schachter also added that staff may want to reach out to the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Horsemen’s Association to inform them of the opportunity to donate to the
equestrian recognition of Jan Ball and Carol Dean-Porter.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
SEPTEMBER 27, 2021
  4
 FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  EQUESTRIAN EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

ACM Davis reported the subcommittee will be meeting and a report will return to the
Commission in the future.

B.  AMBASSADOR PROGRAM

This item will come back to the Committee with more details.

CHAIR HUFF adjourned the Equestrian Committee meeting 8:17 P.M.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

__________________________  __________________________
Alexa Davis  Britt Huff, Chair
Assistant City Manager
